Makes me chuckle every time but... can somebody ELI5 why Stephen Molyneux's "Not an argument" pops up so often? What's the context?

That's his response to any number of fallacious arguments e.g., ad hominem, appeal to authority, circular reasoning, etc.

Perhaps the canonical leftist non-arguments these days are calling Trump and his supporters nazis, or NYtimes citing "anonymous sources" (which is in turned cited by WaPo and a dozen other outlets which all cite one another) without any evidence aside from gossip and hearsay. A sufficient number of outlets doing this form a closed, self-referential epistemological loop which, if repeated loudly and often enough, becomes "truth". This is propaganda 101, and also related to cognitive biases such as the mere exposure effect.

Most (if not all) of the above are designed to appeal to the emotions (generally outrage) and confirmation biases of each publication's respective audiences -- the great majority of whom viscerally hate Trump -- without offering any substantial evidence.

This cuts both ways, as conservatives can just as easily fall into the same traps due to the same biases and fallacies. Therefore, it's good to be aware of both. Nobody is truly objective, but one can strive to be as balanced as possible in their reasoning by becoming familiar with the above.

Situations such as Comey's testimony last week provoke quite a bit of confirmation bias from both Trump's opponents and supporters. In such cases, it might be best to look to the market -- those who've got skin in the game (in addition to ego / one's particular political proclivities) -- for a different take. Investors obviously have their own biases, but given that there wasn't a substantial shift, it's reasonable to conclude that there was no "silver bullet" against Trump, which was the most fervent hope and dream of the democrats.
